title.zh: 第十五 五行三 大水 水變色 大寒 雹 冬雷 山鳴 魚孽 蝗
title.raw: 第十五 五行三 大水 水變色 大寒 雹 冬雷 山鳴 魚孽 蝗 Volume 105: Five Elements Part Three

sentences.zh: 志第十五 五行三

translations.literal: Treatise Fifteen: The Five Elements, Part Three.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Fifteen: The Five Elements, Part Three.

sentences.zh: 大水 水变色 大寒 雹 冬雷 山鸣 鱼孽 蝗

translations.literal: Great floods; water changing color; extreme cold; hail; winter thunder; mountains roaring; fish prodigies; locusts.
translations.idiomatic: This section treats great floods, discolored water, bitter cold, hail, thunder in winter, mountains that thunder, fish omens, and locust swarms.

sentences.zh: 《五行传》曰：「简宗庙，不祷祠，废祭祀，逆天时，则水不润下」谓水失其性而为灾也。

translations.literal: The "Treatise on the Five Elements" says: "When one slights the ancestral shrines, does not pray at the altars, abandons sacrifices, and goes against Heaven's seasons, then water fails to moisten downward"—meaning water loses its proper nature and becomes calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The Hong fan commentary on the Five Elements warns that neglect of the temples, prayer, and seasonal rites—turning one's back on Heaven's calendar—corrupts the virtue of water so it no longer sinks and nourishes the soil, and flood disasters follow.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「听之不聪，是谓不谋。

translations.literal: It also says: "When hearing is not keen, that is called a failure to deliberate."
translations.idiomatic: The same text adds that when the ruler "does not hear clearly," counsel goes unheard—that is the fault called "lack of planning."

sentences.zh: 厥咎急，厥罚恒寒，厥极贫。

translations.literal: Its blame is haste; its scourge is constant cold; its utmost end is destitution.
translations.idiomatic: The omen-chain names rash governance as the moral fault, unrelenting cold as the matching scourge, and grinding poverty as its bitter end.

sentences.zh: 时则有鼓妖，时则有鱼孽，时则有豕祸，时则有耳疴，时则有黑眚、黑祥，惟火沴水。

translations.literal: In such seasons there are drum prodigies, fish prodigies, pig calamities, ailments of the ear, black spectral visitations and black auspices—only fire harms water.
translations.idiomatic: Such ages bring freak drumming, fish omens, swine plagues, ear diseases, and black hauntings—while in the mutual overcoming of phases, fire is said to encroach on water.

sentences.zh: 」鱼孽，刘歆传以为介虫之孽，谓蝗属也。

translations.literal: "Fish prodigies"—Liu Xin's tradition classes them with omens among shelled creatures, meaning the locust kind.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin's school reads "fish prodigies" alongside omens among armored or shelled vermin—in practice, the locust plague.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元元年七月，郡国九大水，伤稼。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongyuan, Emperor He, nine commanderies and kingdoms suffered great floods that injured the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 1 (89 CE), seventh month: nine provinces were inundated and the standing grain was ruined.

sentences.zh: 京房《易传》曰：「颛事有知，诛罚绝理，厥灾水。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's "Tradition of the Changes" says: "When one monopolizes affairs with cunning knowledge, and punishments and executions cut off what is right, the calamity is flood.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang warns that clever, ruthless justice—executions that sever the moral order—calls down flooding as Heaven's rebuke.

sentences.zh: 其水也，雨杀人，陨霜，大风，天黄。

translations.literal: As for that flood: rain kills people; frost falls; great winds; the sky turns yellow.
translations.idiomatic: The portents cluster: lethal downpours, untimely frost, howling gales, and a sallow, yellowed sky.

sentences.zh: 饥而不损，兹谓泰，厥水水杀人。

translations.literal: Famine yet no reduction—this is called "great peace"; its flood is flood that kills people.
translations.idiomatic: When hunger stalks the land yet the court refuses relief—false "tranquility"—the waters rise until they carry off the people.

sentences.zh: 辟遏有德，兹谓狂，厥水水流杀人，已水则地生虫。

translations.literal: Blocking and thwarting the virtuous—this is called madness; its flood is flowing water that kills people, and after the water recedes the ground breeds worms.
translations.idiomatic: To bar worthy men from office is the madness of policy; rivers then run wild and, when they withdraw, leave the fields worm-ridden.

sentences.zh: 归狱不解，兹谓追非，厥水寒杀人。

translations.literal: Cases left in prison without release—this is called pursuing what is wrong; its flood is cold water that kills people.
translations.idiomatic: When the innocent languish in jail, the omen is killing cold carried on the flood.

sentences.zh: 追诛不解，兹谓不理，厥水五谷不收。

translations.literal: Pursuing executions without release—this is called lack of order; its flood is the five grains not gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Endless vindictive killing is "disorder"; the harvest fails and the granaries stand empty.

sentences.zh: 大败不解，兹谓皆阴，厥水流入国邑，陨霜杀谷。

translations.literal: Great defeat without release—this is called all yin; its flood flows into the capital and towns, frost falls and kills the grain.
translations.idiomatic: When a shattering military reverse is never redressed—total yin dominance—rivers invade the cities and late frost finishes the crops.

sentences.zh: 」是时，和帝幼，窦太后摄政，其兄窦宪干事，及宪诸弟皆贵显，并作威虣虐，尝所怨恨，辄任客杀之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor He was young; Empress Dowager Dou held the government; her brother Dou Xian managed affairs, and Xian and his brothers were all noble and prominent, together acting fierce and cruel; whenever they nursed a grudge they would at once employ retainers to murder the object.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was a child; Dou Xian and his kin ran the realm from behind the dowager's screen, swaggering in rank and murdering scores by private assassins whenever spite moved them.

sentences.zh: 其后窦氏诛灭。

translations.literal: Afterward the Dou clan was executed and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In time the whole Dou faction was swept away and put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月，颍川大水，伤稼。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year, Yingchuan suffered a great flood that injured the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 12 (100 CE), sixth month: the Yingchuan plain went under and the harvest was lost.

sentences.zh: 是时，和帝幸邓贵人，阴有欲废阴后之意，阴后亦怀恚怨。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor He favored Worthy Lady Deng and secretly intended to depose Empress Yin; the empress also harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The court had turned to Lady Deng while Empress Yin, sensing she would be cast off, nursed a bitter grudge.

sentences.zh: 一曰，先是恭怀皇后葬礼有阙，窦太后崩后，乃改殡梁后，葬西陵，征舅三人皆为列侯，位特进，赏赐累千金。

translations.literal: One view says: earlier the funeral rites for Empress Gonghuai had been deficient; after Empress Dowager Dou died, they reburied Empress Liang in the west mausoleum and summoned three maternal uncles, all enfeoffed as marquises with special-advance rank, gifts mounting to a thousand catties of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss ties the flood to the shabby obsequies for Empress Gonghuai, the belated reinterment of Empress Liang at Xiling after Dou's death, and the sudden enrichment of three uncles at the highest noble rank.

sentences.zh: 殇帝延平元年五月，郡国三十七大水，伤稼。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yanping, Emperor Shang, thirty-seven commanderies and kingdoms suffered great floods that injured the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Yanping 1 (106 CE), fifth month: thirty-seven provinces flooded and the fields were battered.

sentences.zh: 董仲舒曰：「水者，阴气盛也。

translations.literal: Dong Zhongshu said: "Water means yin qi is abundant."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhongshu read deluge as yin force overwhelming the landscape.

sentences.zh: 」是时，帝在襁抱，邓太后专政。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was in swaddling clothes; Empress Dowager Deng monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: The boy on the throne was still in arms; Empress Dowager Deng held every rein of power.

sentences.zh: 安帝永初元年冬十月辛酉，河南新城山水虣出，突坏民田，坏处泉水出，深三丈。

translations.literal: In the winter, tenth month, on the day xinyou of the first year of Yongchu, Emperor An, mountains and rivers in Xincheng, Henan, burst forth violently, smashed private fields, and where they broke open springs gushed up three zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 1 (107 CE), late autumn: a flash flood out of the Xincheng hills in Henan tore through farmland, and new springs welled ten yards deep in the scour.

sentences.zh: 是时司空周章等以邓太后不立皇太子胜而立清河王子，故谋欲废置。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Zhou Zhang and others, because Empress Dowager Deng had not enthroned Prince Sheng as heir but the prince of Qinghe, therefore plotted to depose and replace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhang and his fellow ministers resented the dowager's choice of the Qinghe infant over Prince Sheng and conspired to reverse the succession.

sentences.zh: 十一月，事觉，章等被诛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the affair was discovered; Zhang and the others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: the plot leaked; Zhou Zhang and his allies went to the block.

sentences.zh: 是年郡国四十一水出，漂没民人。

translations.literal: That year forty-one commanderies and kingdoms had water break out, drifting away and drowning the people.
translations.idiomatic: That same year forty-one jurisdictions saw rivers overrun their banks and sweep away whole communities.

sentences.zh: 《谶》曰：「水者，纯阴之精也。

translations.literal: The "Chen" prophecy says: "Water is the essence of pure yin.
translations.idiomatic: A weft-text declares water the concentrated essence of yin.

sentences.zh: 阴气盛洋溢者，小人专制擅权，妒疾贤者，依公结私，侵乘君子，小人席胜，失怀得志，故涌水为灾。」

translations.literal: When yin qi flourishes and overflows, petty men monopolize power, are jealous of the worthy, rely on public office to pursue private ends, encroach upon gentlemen; petty men sit atop victory, lose restraint and get their will—therefore surging water becomes calamity."
translations.idiomatic: When yin swells past measure, mean men seize the levers of state, envy the good, trade on public trust for private gain, and trample their betters—so the rivers boil up in answer."

sentences.zh: 二年，大水。

translations.literal: The second year: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 2: another year of widespread flooding.

sentences.zh: 三年，大水。

translations.literal: The third year: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 3: floods again.

sentences.zh: 四年，大水。

translations.literal: The fourth year: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 4: the inundations continued.

sentences.zh: 五年，大水。

translations.literal: The fifth year: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 5: still the rivers would not stay their banks.

sentences.zh: 六年，河东池水变色，皆赤如血。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the pools of Hedong changed color, all red as blood.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 6: the ponds of Hedong turned the color of blood.

sentences.zh: 是时，邓太后犹专政。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Deng still monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager's regency still gripped the court.

sentences.zh: 延光三年，大水，流杀民人，伤苗稼。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanguang there was a great flood; flowing water killed the people and injured the seedling crops.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang 3 (124 CE): catastrophic freshets drowned people and laid waste to the young grain.

sentences.zh: 是时安帝信江京、樊丰及阿母王圣等谗言，免太尉杨震，废皇太子。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor An believed the slander of Jiang Jing, Fan Feng, and his nurse Wang Sheng and the like, dismissed Grand Commandant Yang Zhen, and deposed the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor listened to his eunuchs and his wet nurse, cashiered Yang Zhen, and cast down the crown prince—classic signs of a tottering house.

sentences.zh: 质帝本初元年五月，海水溢乐安、北海，溺杀人、物。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Benchu, Emperor Zhi, the sea overflowed Le'an and Beihai, drowning people and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Benchu 1 (146 CE), fifth month: the Bohai tide surged into Le'an and Beihai, swallowing lives and property.

sentences.zh: 是时帝幼，梁太后专政。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was young; Empress Dowager Liang monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: Another child emperor; the Liang empress dowager held the regency.

sentences.zh: 桓帝建和二年七月，京师大水。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jianhe, Emperor Huan, the capital suffered a great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Jianhe 2 (148 CE), seventh month: Luoyang was awash.

sentences.zh: 去年冬，梁冀枉杀故太尉李固、杜乔。

translations.literal: The previous winter Liang Ji had unjustly killed the former Grand Commandants Li Gu and Du Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Only months after Liang Ji had framed and executed the two grand commandants Li Gu and Du Qiao.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，京都大水。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year the capital suffered a great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Jianhe 3, eighth month: the capital flooded again.

sentences.zh: 是时，梁太后犹专政。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Liang still monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang dowager still pulled every string from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 永兴元年秋，河水溢，漂害人、物。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Yongxing the Yellow River overflowed, drifting away and injuring people and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing 1 (153 CE), autumn: the great river burst its dikes and carried off people and stores.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，彭城泗水增长，逆流。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year the Si River in Pengcheng rose and flowed backward.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing 2, sixth month: the Si swelled so violently at Pengcheng that it ran upstream.

sentences.zh: 永寿元年六月，雒水溢至津阳城门，漂流人、物。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Yongshou the Luo River overflowed to the Jinyang city gate, drifting away people and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshou 1 (155 CE), sixth month: the Luo climbed to the Jinyang gate, rafting debris and bodies through the streets.

sentences.zh: 是时梁皇后兄冀秉政，疾害忠直，威权震主。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Liang's brother Ji held power, hated and injured the loyal and straight, and his awesomeness shook the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ji, the empress's brother, dominated the bureaucracy, hunted the outspoken, and terrified even the throne.

sentences.zh: 后遂诛灭。

translations.literal: Afterward he was executed and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He and his clan were extirpated not long after.

sentences.zh: 延熹八年四月，济北河水清。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Yanxi the Yellow River in Jibei ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi 8 (165 CE), fourth month: the Ji-north reach of the Yellow River ran transparent—a freak omen.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，济阴、东郡、济北、平原河水清。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year Jiyin, Dongjun, Jibei, and Pingyuan Yellow River water ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: Next year's fourth month: the same uncanny clarity appeared along the Yellow River in four commanderies.

sentences.zh: 襄楷上言：「河者诸侯之象，清者阳明之征，岂独诸侯有规京都计邪？

translations.literal: Xiang Kai submitted a memorial: "The river is the image of the feudal lords; clarity is the sign of yang brightness—does it mean only that the lords are taking aim at the capital's plans?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Kai warned the throne that rivers stand for the regional kings and limpid water for aggressive yang—were the provinces sizing up Luoyang?

sentences.zh: 」其明年，宫车晏驾，征解犊亭侯为汉嗣，即尊位，是为孝灵皇帝。

translations.literal: The next year the imperial carriage delayed; the Marquis of Jieduting was summoned to continue Han; he assumed the supreme position—this was Emperor Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Huan died without issue; the court fetched Liu Hong, marquis of Jieduting, who ascended as Emperor Ling.

sentences.zh: 永康元年八月，六州大水，勃海海溢，没杀人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongkang six provinces suffered great floods; the Bohai sea overflowed and drowned people.
translations.idiomatic: Yongkang 1 (167 CE), eighth month: six provinces drowned; the Bohai tide rolled inland and killed many.

sentences.zh: 是时，桓帝奢侈淫祀，其十一月崩，无嗣。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Huan practiced extravagance and wanton sacrifice; in the eleventh month he died without heir.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had bankrupted the treasury on shrines and pleasures; he died childless that winter.

sentences.zh: 灵帝建宁四年二月，河水清。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Jianning, Emperor Ling, the Yellow River ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: Jianning 4 (171 CE), second month: again the Yellow River ran crystal-clear.

sentences.zh: 五月，山水大出，漂坏庐舍五百余家。

translations.literal: In the fifth month mountains and rivers burst forth greatly, drifting away and destroying more than five hundred homes.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: mountain torrents smashed over five hundred dwellings.

sentences.zh: 熹平二年六月，东莱、北海海水溢出，漂没人物。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Xiping Donglai and Beihai sea water overflowed, drifting away and drowning people and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Xiping 2 (173 CE), sixth month: the sea breached Donglai and Beihai, wiping out lives and goods.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，雒水出。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year the Luo River came out.
translations.idiomatic: Xiping 3, autumn: the Luo left its channel.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，郡国三水，伤害秋稼。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year three commanderies and kingdoms had flood; it injured the autumn crops.
translations.idiomatic: Xiping 4, summer: three jurisdictions flooded and the late-season grain was spoiled.

sentences.zh: 光和六年秋，金城河溢，水出二十余里。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year of Guanghe the Jinzhou Yellow River overflowed; water came out more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghe 6 (183 CE), autumn: the Jinzhou reach of the Yellow River spread miles beyond its banks.

sentences.zh: 中平五年，郡国六水大出。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhongping six commanderies and kingdoms had water break out greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongping 5 (188 CE): six provinces were hit by major cloudbursts and river bursts.

sentences.zh: 献帝建安二年九月，汉水流，害民人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Jian'an, Emperor Xian, the Han River flowed, injuring the people.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an 2 (197 CE), ninth month: the Han River rampaged through settled country.

sentences.zh: 是时，天下大乱。

translations.literal: At that time all under Heaven was in great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was already torn by warlord strife.

sentences.zh: 十八年六月，大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighteenth year: great flood.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an 18, sixth month: another great inundation.

sentences.zh: 二十四年八月，汉水溢流，害民人。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-fourth year the Han River overflowed and flowed, injuring the people.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an 24, eighth month: the Han rose again and drowned communities along its course.

sentences.zh: 庶征之恒寒。

translations.literal: Among the "Various Signs"—constant cold.
translations.idiomatic: Under the heading of miscellaneous portents comes unseasonable, enduring cold.

sentences.zh: 灵帝光和六年冬，大寒，北海、东莱、琅邪井中冰厚尺余。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Guanghe, Emperor Ling, extreme cold; in Beihai, Donglai, and Langye ice in the wells was more than a chi thick.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghe 6, winter: a killing frost gripped the coast—wells in Beihai, Donglai, and Langye froze over a foot thick.

sentences.zh: 献帝初平四年六月，寒风如冬时。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Chuping, Emperor Xian, cold wind as in wintertime.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping 4 (193 CE), sixth month: a blast swept the land as bitter as mid-winter.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元五年六月，郡国三雨雹，大如鸡子。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Yongyuan, Emperor He, three commanderies and kingdoms rained hail as large as chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 5 (93 CE), sixth month: hailstones the size of eggs fell across three provinces.

sentences.zh: 是时和帝用酷吏周纡为司隶校尉，刑诛深刻。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor He employed the cruel official Zhou Xu as Metropolitan Superintendent; punishments and executions were deep and severe.
translations.idiomatic: He had put the notorious Zhou Xu in charge of the capital corps; torture and summary execution became the norm.

sentences.zh: 安帝永初元年，雨雹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu, Emperor An: it rained hail.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 1: hailstorms swept the north.

sentences.zh: 二年，雨雹，大如鸡子。

translations.literal: The second year: it rained hail, large as chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 2: egg-sized hail returned.

sentences.zh: 三年，雨雹，大如雁子，伤稼。

translations.literal: The third year: it rained hail, large as goose eggs, injuring the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 3: hail as big as goose eggs beat down the standing grain.

sentences.zh: 刘向以为雹，阴胁阳也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang held that hail means yin threatening yang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang read hail as yin force lashing out at yang.

sentences.zh: 是时邓太后以阴专阳政。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Deng used yin to monopolize yang's government.
translations.idiomatic: A woman regent, in Liu Xiang's cosmology, was yin ruling in yang's place.

sentences.zh: 元初四年六月戊辰，郡国三雨雹，大如杅杯及鸡子，杀六畜。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen in the sixth month of the fourth year of Yuanchu three commanderies and kingdoms rained hail, large as pestle-cups and chicken eggs, killing the six kinds of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchu 4 (117 CE), sixth month, wuchen: three provinces were pelted with hail between cup- and egg-size; herds died in the fields.

sentences.zh: 延光元年四月，郡国二十一雨雹，大如鸡子，伤稼。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yanguang twenty-one commanderies and kingdoms rained hail, large as chicken eggs, injuring the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang 1 (122 CE), fourth month: twenty-one jurisdictions caught egg-sized hail that shredded the crops.

sentences.zh: 是时安帝信谗，无辜死者多。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor An believed slander; many died without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again lent his ear to informers; innocents perished wholesale.

sentences.zh: 三年，雨雹，大如鸡子。

translations.literal: The third year: it rained hail, large as chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang 3: another season of egg-sized hail.

sentences.zh: 桓帝延熹四年五月己卯，京都雨雹，大如鸡子。

translations.literal: On the day jimao in the fifth month of the fourth year of Yanxi, Emperor Huan, the capital rained hail, large as chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi 4 (161 CE), fifth month, jimao: Luoyang was bombarded with hail as large as eggs.

sentences.zh: 是时，桓帝诛杀过差，又宠小人。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Huan's executions exceeded what was right, and he also favored petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was slaughtering beyond measure while showering favor on sycophants.

sentences.zh: 七年五月己丑，京都雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day jichou in the fifth month of the seventh year the capital rained hail.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi 7 (164 CE), fifth month, jichou: the capital hailstorm returned.

sentences.zh: 是时，皇后邓氏僭侈，骄恣专幸。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Deng acted beyond her rank, was arrogant and unrestrained, and monopolized favor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Deng had grown haughty, extravagant, and jealous of every rival for the emperor's eye.

sentences.zh: 明年废，以忧死，其家皆诛。

translations.literal: The next year she was deposed, died of grief, and her family were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year she was cast down, broken-hearted, and her kin extirpated.

sentences.zh: 灵帝建宁二年四月，雨雹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Jianning, Emperor Ling: it rained hail.
translations.idiomatic: Jianning 2 (169 CE), fourth month: hail.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，河东雨雹。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year Hedong rained hail.
translations.idiomatic: Jianning 4, fifth month: Hedong was hail-struck.

sentences.zh: 光和四年六月，雨雹，大如鸡子。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Guanghe it rained hail, large as chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghe 4 (181 CE), sixth month: egg-sized hail again.

sentences.zh: 是时，常侍、黄门用权。

translations.literal: At that time the regular attendants and Yellow Gates employed power.
translations.idiomatic: The palace eunuchs held the real authority.

sentences.zh: 中平二年四月庚戌，雨雹，伤稼。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu in the fourth month of the second year of Zhongping it rained hail, injuring the crops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongping 2 (185 CE), fourth month, gengxu: hail ruined the spring planting.

sentences.zh: 献帝初平四年六月，右扶风雹如斗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Chuping, Emperor Xian, in Youfufeng hail like dou measures.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping 4, sixth month: west of the capital, hail fell in lumps the size of peck measures.

sentences.zh: 和帝元兴元年冬十一月壬午，郡国四冬雷。

translations.literal: On the day renwu in the eleventh month of the winter of the first year of Yuanxing, Emperor He, four commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxing 1 (105 CE), eleventh month, renwu: thunder rolled in winter across four provinces—an uncanny sound.

sentences.zh: 是时皇子数不遂，皆隐之民间。

translations.literal: At that time imperial sons repeatedly did not succeed; all were hidden among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Several imperial infants had died in secret; the court hid the losses from the realm.

sentences.zh: 是岁，宫车晏驾，殇帝生百余日，立以为君；

translations.literal: That year the imperial carriage delayed; Emperor Shang, born a hundred-odd days, was set up as lord;
translations.idiomatic: When He died that year the throne passed to the hundred-day-old Shang;

sentences.zh: 帝兄有疾，封为平原王，卒，皆夭无嗣。

translations.literal: the emperor's elder brother was ill, enfeoffed as prince of Pingyuan, died—all were young without posterity.
translations.idiomatic: the sick elder prince of Pingyuan followed him to the grave—He's line seemed cursed to die young and heirless.

sentences.zh: 殇帝延平元年九月乙亥，陈留雷，有石陨地四。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on the day yihai of the first year of Yanping, Emperor Shang, Chenliu thundered, and stones fell to the ground—four.
translations.idiomatic: Yanping 1, ninth month, yihai: thunder over Chenliu shook four stones from the sky.

sentences.zh: 安帝永初六年十月丙戌，郡六冬雷。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu in the tenth month of the sixth year of Yongchu, Emperor An, six commanderies had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 6 (112 CE), tenth month, bingxu: winter thunder in six commanderies.

sentences.zh: 七年十月戊子，郡国三冬雷。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi in the tenth month of the seventh year three commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 7, tenth month, wuzi: three more provinces heard thunder in the dead of winter.

sentences.zh: 元初元年十月癸巳，郡国三冬雷。

translations.literal: On the day guisi in the tenth month of the first year of Yuanchu three commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchu 1 (114 CE), tenth month, guisi: triple winter thunder omen.

sentences.zh: 三年十月辛亥，汝南、乐浪冬雷。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai in the tenth month of the third year Ru'nan and Lelang had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchu 3, tenth month, xinhai: Ru'nan and Lelang echoed with winter peals.

sentences.zh: 四年十月辛酉，郡国五冬雷。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou in the tenth month of the fourth year five commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchu 4, tenth month, xinyou: five jurisdictions lit up with off-season thunder.

sentences.zh: 六年十月丙子，郡国五冬雷。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi in the tenth month of the sixth year five commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchu 6 (119 CE), tenth month, bingzi: winter thunder rolled across five provinces.

sentences.zh: 永宁元年十月，郡国七冬雷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongning seven commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning 1 (120 CE), tenth month: seven jurisdictions heard thunder out of season.

sentences.zh: 建光元年十月，郡国七冬雷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Jianguang seven commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Jianguang 1 (121 CE), tenth month: the same omen struck seven provinces again.

sentences.zh: 延光四年，郡国十九冬雷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanguang nineteen commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang 4 (125 CE): nineteen commanderies reported winter thunder—a widespread sign.

sentences.zh: 是时，太后摄政，上无所与。

translations.literal: At that time the empress dowager held the government; the emperor participated in nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager regent ran every decision; the sovereign had no voice in affairs.

sentences.zh: 太后既崩，阿母王圣及皇后兄阎显兄弟更秉威权，上遂不亲万机，从容宽仁任臣下。

translations.literal: After the empress dowager died, the nurse Wang Sheng and the empress's elder brothers Yan Xian and company in turn grasped awesome power; the emperor thereupon did not personally attend to the myriad threads of state, but was easygoing, lenient, and entrusted things to his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, the emperor's wet nurse Wang Sheng and Empress Yan's brothers seized the reins; the ruler withdrew from the daily grind of government, indulged a reputation for mildness, and left policy to his officials.

sentences.zh: 桓帝建和三年六月乙卯，雷震宪陵寝屋。

translations.literal: On the day yimao in the sixth month of the third year of Jianhe, Emperor Huan, thunder struck the roof of the sleeping hall at Xian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Jianhe 3 (149 CE), sixth month, yimao: lightning shattered the roof of the tomb hall at Emperor Zhang's Xianling.

sentences.zh: 先是梁太后听兄冀枉杀李固、杜乔。

translations.literal: Earlier Empress Dowager Liang had listened to her brother Ji and unjustly killed Li Gu and Du Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: The bolt answered Liang Ji's earlier murder of Grand Commandants Li Gu and Du Qiao at his sister's behest.

sentences.zh: 灵帝熹平六年冬十月，东莱冬雷。

translations.literal: In the winter tenth month of the sixth year of Xiping, Emperor Ling, Donglai had winter thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiping 6 (177 CE), winter: thunder rolled over Donglai though snow should have sealed the sky.

sentences.zh: 中平四年十二月晦，雨水，大雷电。

translations.literal: On the last day of the twelfth month of the fourth year of Zhongping there was rain water, great thunder and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongping 4 (187 CE), month's end: warm rain fell with deafening thunder—freak weather for deep winter.

sentences.zh: 雹。

translations.literal: Hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hail followed—a further portent in the same season.

sentences.zh: 献帝初平三年五月丙申，无云而雷。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen in the fifth month of the third year of Chuping, Emperor Xian, there was thunder though no clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping 3 (192 CE), fifth month, bingshen: thunder pealed from a clear sky.

sentences.zh: 四年五月癸酉，无云而雷。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou in the fifth month of the fourth year there was thunder though no clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Chuping 4, fifth month, guiyou: again thunder without a cloud in sight.

sentences.zh: 建安七八年中，长沙醴陵县有大山，常大鸣如牛呴声，积数年。

translations.literal: In the seventh and eighth years of Jian'an there was a great mountain in Liling county, Changsha, which often roared greatly like the sound of an ox lowing, accumulating for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Between Jian'an 7 and 8 (202–203 CE) a peak above Liling in Changsha lowed like a bull for years on end.

sentences.zh: 后豫章贼攻没醴陵县，杀略吏民。

translations.literal: Afterward Yuzhang bandits attacked and overran Liling county, killing and plundering officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Then bandits from Yuzhang stormed Liling, slaughtering and looting the county.

sentences.zh: 灵帝熹平二年，东莱海出大鱼二枚，长八九丈，高二丈余。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiping, Emperor Ling, two great fish came forth from the sea at Donglai, eight or nine zhang in length and more than two zhang in height.
translations.idiomatic: Xiping 2 (173 CE): two leviathans surfaced off Donglai—ninety feet long and twenty feet out of the water.

sentences.zh: 明年，中山王暢、任城王博并薨。

translations.literal: The next year the prince of Zhongshan, Chang, and the prince of Rencheng, Bo, both died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year two imperial princes, Chang of Zhongshan and Bo of Rencheng, died the same year.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元四年，蝗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongyuan, Emperor He: locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 4 (92 CE): locust clouds darkened the fields.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，河内、陈留蝗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year Henei and Chenliu had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 8, fifth month: the pests devoured Henei and Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 九月，京都蝗。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the capital had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: the swarm reached Luoyang itself.

sentences.zh: 九年，蝗从夏至秋。

translations.literal: In the ninth year locusts ran from summer through autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 9: the infestation lasted from midsummer into fall.

sentences.zh: 先是，西羌数反，遣将军将北军五校征之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Western Qiang had repeatedly rebelled; generals were dispatched with the Northern Army's five camps to chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: For years the Western Qiang had risen in revolt, drawing expedition after expedition from the capital legions.

sentences.zh: 安帝永初四年夏，蝗。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Yongchu, Emperor An: locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 4 (110 CE), summer: locusts again.

sentences.zh: 是时，西羌寇乱，军众征距，连十余年。

translations.literal: At that time the Western Qiang raided and threw the frontier into turmoil; armies marched and countermarched for more than ten years linked together.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang war had dragged on for over a decade of campaigning.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，九州蝗。

translations.literal: In the fifth year summer the nine provinces had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 5, summer: the plague of locusts spread across all nine provinces.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，去蝗处复蝗子生。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year where the locusts had gone locust larvae were born again.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 6, third month: the stripped fields hatched a second brood of hoppers.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，蝗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year summer: locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchu 7, summer: another wave of locusts.

sentences.zh: 元初元年夏，郡国五蝗。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Yuanchu five commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchu 1 (114 CE), summer: five commanderies were stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，郡国二十蝗。

translations.literal: In the second year summer twenty commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchu 2, summer: twenty jurisdictions reported swarms.

sentences.zh: 延光元年六月，郡国蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Yanguang commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang 1 (122 CE), sixth month: a general locust plague.

sentences.zh: 顺帝永建五年，郡国十二蝗。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongjian, Emperor Shun, twelve commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjian 5 (130 CE): twelve provinces suffered locusts.

sentences.zh: 是时，鲜卑寇朔方，用众征之。

translations.literal: At that time the Xianbei raided Shuofang; troops were mobilized to chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei were probing Shuofang; the court sent a punitive host north.

sentences.zh: 永和元年秋七月。

translations.literal: Yonghe 1: the seventh month of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe 1 (136 CE), late summer heading into autumn—the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 偃师蝗。

translations.literal: Yanshi had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts fell on Yanshi east of the capital.

sentences.zh: 去年冬，乌桓寇沙南，用众征之。

translations.literal: The previous winter the Wuhuan had raided Shanan; troops were mobilized to chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: That followed a winter campaign against Wuhuan incursions south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 桓帝永兴元年七月，郡国三十二蝗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongxing, Emperor Huan, thirty-two commanderies and kingdoms had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing 1 (153 CE), seventh month: thirty-two commanderies writhed under locusts.

sentences.zh: 是时，梁冀秉政无谋宪，苟贪权作虐。

translations.literal: At that time Liang Ji held power without regard for fundamental norms, greedily grasping authority and committing cruelties.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ji ruled with no respect for law or counsel—only a cruel grip on power.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，京都蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year the capital had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing 2, sixth month: the capital itself was swarmed.

sentences.zh: 永寿三年六月，京都蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Yongshou the capital had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshou 3 (157 CE), sixth month: Luoyang again under locusts.

sentences.zh: 延熹元年五月，京都蝗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yanxi the capital had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi 1 (158 CE), fifth month: another locust year in the capital.

sentences.zh: 灵帝熹平六年夏，七州蝗。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year of Xiping seven provinces had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiping 6 (177 CE), summer: seven provinces were eaten bare.

sentences.zh: 先是，鲜卑前后三十余犯塞。

translations.literal: Earlier the Xianbei had violated the frontier more than thirty times in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei had raided the passes over thirty times running.

sentences.zh: 是岁，护乌桓校尉夏育、破鲜卑中郎将田晏、使匈奴中郎将臧旻将南单于以下，三道并出讨鲜卑。

translations.literal: That year the Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan Xia Yu, the General Breaking the Xianbei Tian Yan, and the Commissioner over the Xianbei Zang Min, leading the Southern Shanyu and those below, set out on three routes together to punish the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: The court launched a three-pronged expedition—Xia Yu, Tian Yan, and Zang Min at the head of Wuhuan auxiliaries, Southern Xiongnu allies, and frontier garrisons—to crush the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 大司农经用不足，殷敛郡国，以给军粮。

translations.literal: The Grand Minister of Agriculture's regular funds were insufficient; he pressed levies on commanderies and kingdoms to supply military grain.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury ran dry; ministers squeezed every commandery for grain to feed the armies.

sentences.zh: 三将无功，还者少半。

translations.literal: The three generals achieved no success; of those who returned fewer than half.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign failed; fewer than half the men came back.

sentences.zh: 献帝兴平元年夏，大蝗。

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Xingping, Emperor Xian, great locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Xingping 1 (194 CE), summer: locusts blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 是时，天下大乱。

translations.literal: At that time all under Heaven was in great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was already torn by warlords and famine.

sentences.zh: 建安二年五月，蝗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Jian'an: locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an 2 (197 CE), fifth month: the hoppers returned.
